concepts.name: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin
concepts.summary: Recall the three temperature scales, convert between them, and identify absolute zero as the zero of the Kelvin scale.

concepts.name: Temperature and thermal equilibrium
concepts.summary: Explain that temperature determines the direction of heat flow and that objects in thermal equilibrium share the same temperature, as stated by the zeroth law.

concepts.name: Heat versus temperature
concepts.summary: Distinguish heat as energy transferred because of a temperature difference from temperature as a measure of thermal state.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity
concepts.summary: Explain that different materials need different amounts of heat per unit mass to change temperature, and relate this to Q = mcΔT.

concepts.name: Latent heat and phase change
concepts.summary: Describe how heat absorbed or released during melting, boiling or freezing changes the phase without changing the temperature.

concepts.name: Heat transfer modes
concepts.summary: Name and describe conduction, convection and radiation as ways thermal energy moves.

concepts.name: Pressure, volume and temperature of gases
concepts.summary: Describe a gas by its pressure, volume, temperature and amount, and explain qualitatively how they change together.

misconceptions.text: Heat and temperature are the same thing.
Adding heat to a substance always raises its temperature.
Cold is a substance that flows from one object to another, instead of heat flowing from hot to cold.

concepts.name: Ideal gas law
concepts.summary: Apply PV = nRT with absolute temperature to find an unknown state variable for a gas sample.

concepts.name: Calorimetry problems
concepts.summary: Use energy conservation with specific and latent heats to find final temperatures or masses when bodies exchange heat.

concepts.name: Work done by expanding gas
concepts.summary: Compute work for constant-pressure changes as PΔV and interpret it as area under a pV diagram.

concepts.name: First law of thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Apply ΔU = Q − W with consistent sign conventions to track heat, work and internal energy of a system.

concepts.name: Internal energy of ideal gas
concepts.summary: Explain that internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature and relates to molecular kinetic energy.

concepts.name: Molar heat capacities Cv and Cp
concepts.summary: Use Cv and Cp to compute heat for constant-volume and constant-pressure processes and explain why Cp exceeds Cv.

concepts.name: Reading pV diagrams
concepts.summary: Identify isobaric, isochoric and other processes on a pV diagram and read off work and state changes.

misconceptions.text: The ideal gas law can be used with temperature in Celsius.
Work done by a gas is always positive regardless of the sign convention or whether it expands or compresses.
Heat and work are properties stored in a system, like internal energy.

concepts.name: Isothermal process analysis
concepts.summary: Compute work W = nRT ln(V2/V1) and show that heat in equals work out for an ideal gas isotherm.

concepts.name: Adiabatic process analysis
concepts.summary: Use PV^γ = constant and TV^(γ−1) = constant to find states and work when no heat is exchanged.

concepts.name: Heat engine and efficiency
concepts.summary: Compute efficiency as net work over heat input for a cycle and account for heat rejected to a cold reservoir.

concepts.name: Refrigerators and heat pumps
concepts.summary: Calculate coefficients of performance for refrigerators and heat pumps from heat and work flows.

concepts.name: Second law statements
concepts.summary: Analyse the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements and show their equivalence and what they forbid.

concepts.name: Reversible and irreversible processes
concepts.summary: Distinguish reversible idealisations from real irreversible processes and identify sources of irreversibility such as friction and finite temperature differences.

concepts.name: Entropy change calculation
concepts.summary: Compute entropy changes for heating, phase changes and ideal gas processes using dS = dQ_rev/T.

concepts.name: Carnot cycle
concepts.summary: Analyse the four steps of the Carnot cycle and derive its efficiency 1 − Tc/Th.

misconceptions.text: In an isothermal ideal gas process, no heat flows because the temperature is constant.
A heat engine can reach 100% efficiency if friction is eliminated.
Adiabatic means isothermal, so temperature stays constant.

concepts.name: Entropy increase principle
concepts.summary: Use total entropy change of system plus surroundings to decide whether a process is reversible, irreversible or impossible.

concepts.name: Carnot theorem and bounds
concepts.summary: Evaluate real engines and refrigerators against the Carnot limit and justify why no engine between two reservoirs can beat it.

concepts.name: Boltzmann microstate entropy
concepts.summary: Relate entropy to the number of microstates via S = k ln W and explain macrostates as collections of microstates.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic potentials
concepts.summary: Choose among internal energy, enthalpy, Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies to predict spontaneity under given constraints.

concepts.name: Free expansion and mixing entropy
concepts.summary: Calculate entropy generated in irreversible free expansion and mixing by constructing a reversible path between the same states.

concepts.name: Third law and absolute entropy
concepts.summary: Explain that entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero at absolute zero and that absolute zero cannot be reached in finitely many steps.

concepts.name: Temperature-entropy diagrams
concepts.summary: Use TS diagrams to read heat as area and compare cycles, identifying isentropic and isothermal segments.

concepts.name: Real engine cycles
concepts.summary: Analyse Otto-type and similar cycles on pV or TS diagrams to derive efficiencies and locate losses.

misconceptions.text: Entropy can never decrease anywhere, even within a subsystem.
Entropy is simply a measure of visible messiness rather than a count of accessible microstates.
Entropy does not change in a free expansion because no heat is exchanged.

concepts.name: Statistical ensembles and partition function
concepts.summary: Evaluate how the partition function generates thermodynamic quantities such as energy, entropy and free energy from microscopic spectra.

concepts.name: Gibbs entropy and information
concepts.summary: Assess the equivalence between Gibbs entropy −kΣp ln p and information-theoretic entropy and its role in resolving Maxwell's demon.

concepts.name: Second law and arrow of time
concepts.summary: Critically evaluate how time-reversible microscopic laws coexist with the statistical, probabilistic irreversibility of the second law.

concepts.name: Maxwell relations and response functions
concepts.summary: Derive relations among response functions such as Cp − Cv and compressibilities from potentials via Legendre transformation and Maxwell relations.

concepts.name: Finite-time and nonequilibrium engines
concepts.summary: Evaluate efficiency at maximum power for engines with finite heat transfer rates and contrast it with Carnot efficiency.

concepts.name: Phase transition thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Evaluate phase coexistence and transitions using Gibbs free energy, the Clausius-Clapeyron relation and critical behaviour.

concepts.name: Design of thermodynamic systems
concepts.summary: Design or optimise a thermal system using exergy and entropy generation analysis to justify trade-offs between efficiency, cost and irreversibility.

concepts.name: Fluctuation theorems
concepts.summary: Construct arguments for how fluctuation theorems extend the second law to small systems far from equilibrium.

misconceptions.text: The second law is an absolute dynamical law that forbids any entropy-decreasing fluctuation in any system.
Carnot efficiency is the practical target for engines operating at maximum power.
Information entropy and thermodynamic entropy are unrelated, merely sharing a name.
